Faq.title: SunEditor at a glance
Faq.desc: Short answers to the questions developers ask before choosing an editor.

commercial.q: Is SunEditor free for commercial use?
commercial.a: Yes. SunEditor is released under the MIT License. You can use it in commercial products, SaaS and internal tools, modify it and self-host it. Keep the copyright and license notice in your copies. There is no license key, account or per-load fee.

dependencies.a: No. The suneditor package has zero runtime dependencies. Optional integrations such as KaTeX or MathJax (math) and CodeMirror (code view) are used only if you enable them.

frameworks.q: Which frameworks does it work with?
frameworks.a: SunEditor is plain JavaScript, so it works anywhere a browser runs: vanilla JS via npm or CDN, React, Vue, Angular, Svelte and Web Components. TypeScript type definitions are included in the package.

features.q: What is included out of the box?
features.a: Tables with cell merge and split, image, video, audio and file upload, links, math, code blocks, Markdown view, drawing, templates and layouts, slash commands and block handles — 30+ plugins in total, plus 25+ language packs and RTL support. All plugins ship in one package — enable only the ones you need with the plugins option.

cloud.q: Does it require a cloud service or an account?
cloud.a: No. The editor runs entirely in the browser and does not send your content to any external service. Uploads go to an endpoint on your own server, set with the uploadUrl option.

output.a: Standard HTML. To display saved content with the same styles as the editor, import suneditor/css/contents and wrap the HTML in an element with the sun-editor-editable class.

DeepDive.title: Deep Dive
DeepDive.subtitle: Custom themes, upload integration, and event callbacks for SunEditor v3.

theme.builtInThemesDesc: SunEditor ships with 4 built-in themes. Import the CSS file and pass the theme name to options.
theme.cssVariablesDesc: Each theme defines ~130 CSS custom properties organized into categories. Override them to customize any part of the editor.

varDesc.contentArea: Colors for the editable content area (text, backgrounds, borders)
varDesc.layoutShell: Toolbar, statusbar, and outer shell styling
varDesc.modalDropdown: Dialog modals, dropdowns, and controller surfaces
varDesc.statusColors: Success/error feedback colors and loading indicators

theme.totalVars: Total: ~130 CSS variables per theme. Copy a built-in theme as your starting point and modify the colors.
theme.customThemeDesc: Create a CSS file that defines all variables under your theme's selector. The class name must follow the pattern: se-theme-'{'name'}'.
theme.step1Desc: Define all CSS variables under .sun-editor.se-theme-'{'name'}' and .sun-editor-editable.se-theme-'{'name'}' selectors.
theme.step2Desc: Import the CSS file in your app and set the theme option to match your theme name.
theme.tip1: Copy an existing theme (e.g. dark.css) as your base — it has all required variables.
theme.tip2: The selector must include both .sun-editor.se-theme-'{'name'}' (UI) and .sun-editor-editable.se-theme-'{'name'}' (content).
theme.tip3: Use setTheme() to switch themes at runtime without recreating the editor.
theme.tip4: Theme CSS is additive — unlisted variables fall back to the default theme.

events.overviewDesc: SunEditor provides 35+ event callbacks covering lifecycle, input, clipboard, media upload, and UI interactions. Assign a function to the event property to handle it.
events.basicEventsDesc: Core events for initialization, content changes, and save operations.
events.inputEventsDesc: Intercept and control text input and keyboard events. Return false to prevent default behavior.
events.clipboardEventsDesc: Handle paste and drop events with content filtering. Return false to cancel, or a string to replace content.
events.imageEventsDesc: Full control over image upload lifecycle — validate before upload, track loaded images, handle errors. Same pattern applies to video/audio/file.
events.focusEventsDesc: SunEditor has both managed focus (onFocus/onBlur) and native DOM focus events. Use managed events for most cases.
events.focusTipDesc: Use onFocus/onBlur for most cases — they fire after toolbar updates and status flags are set. Use onNativeFocus/onNativeBlur only when you need to intercept the raw browser event before SunEditor processes it.
events.uiEventsDesc: Respond to toolbar visibility, code view toggle, fullscreen, and editor resize.

inspector.title: Live Event Inspector
inspector.desc: Interact with the editor on the left and watch every event fire in real time on the right. Click a row to expand its payload.
inspector.empty: No events yet — start typing or click a toolbar button.
inspector.returnTrueNote: This event treats undefined as "handled" and stops the upload. A passive listener must return true.
inspector.notAttachedDesc: Upload handlers take over the upload response — attaching a logger would stop uploaded media from being inserted — so the inspector leaves them alone:

upload.overviewDesc: SunEditor supports file upload for images, videos, audio, and generic files. Each media type has its own upload URL, event hooks, and optional custom handler.
upload.optionsDesc: Set upload URL, size limits, accepted formats, and headers for each media type.
upload.serverResponseDesc: Your upload server must return JSON in this format. SunEditor sends files as multipart/form-data with field name 'file-0', 'file-1', etc.
upload.customHandlerDesc: Use imageUploadHandler when your upload API returns a different response format. SunEditor still sends the request; once the handler is defined, it receives the finished request and decides what to insert — the built-in insertion is skipped.
upload.customHandlerDirectLink: Upload straight to S3 or other storage instead
upload.validationDesc: Use *UploadBefore events to validate or modify files before they're sent to the server. Works for all media types.
upload.errorsDesc: Customize error messages shown to users when uploads fail. Return a string to override the default message.
upload.lifecycleDesc: Track when media is created, updated, or deleted. Use onFileManagerAction for unified tracking across all types, or per-type events for specific handling.
upload.imageResizeDesc: Large photos from phone cameras can be 10MB+. Resizing on the client before upload reduces bandwidth costs and server CPU load. Use the Canvas API in onImageUploadBefore to downscale images — SVG and animated GIF are skipped since they can't be rasterized meaningfully.
upload.imageResizeNote: The server should still enforce its own size limit as a safety net. Client-side resize is an optimization, not a replacement for server validation.
upload.fileManagementUIDesc: SunEditor fires onFileManagerAction whenever media is created, updated, or deleted — regardless of plugin type. By tracking these events in a state array, you can build a panel that shows all uploaded files with actions like select (scroll to the element in the editor) and delete.
upload.fileManagementUINote: info.delete() and info.select() are closures provided by SunEditor. Calling info.delete() removes the element from the editor and triggers the delete event again, so the list stays in sync automatically.

DocsApi.title: API Reference
DocsApi.editorInstanceDesc: The editor instance contains the Core ($), the internal engine that powers all subsystems. Access it via editor.$ — e.g. editor.$.store, editor.$.selection, editor.$.format, etc.
DocsApi.layerL1Desc: The foundational layer of the core. facade is a back-reference to the public Editor instance (the object returned by SunEditor.create()), and store is the central state management system with subscription support.
DocsApi.kernelInfoDesc: The Core ($) is the internal engine of SunEditor. It is structured in layers: L2 Config providers initialize first, then L3 Logic subsystems are constructed with those providers injected. All subsystems are accessible via editor.$ (e.g. editor.$.selection, editor.$.format).
DocsApi.layerL2Desc: Configuration providers initialized in Phase 1. contextProvider and optionProvider manage global/frame contexts and options, instanceCheck enables iframe-safe type checks, and eventManager provides the public event API.
DocsApi.layerL2AccDesc: Convenience getter properties on $ that provide direct access to frequently-used configuration data from contextProvider and optionProvider — such as DOM references (context, frameContext), editor settings (options, frameOptions), and UI resources (icons, lang).
DocsApi.layerL3DomDesc: DOM manipulation and content analysis subsystems. Provides a unified abstraction over contentEditable: offset calculates positions, selection manages ranges, format handles block-level structure, inline applies character-level styling, html sanitizes content, and char enforces character limits.
DocsApi.layerL3ShellDesc: Editor operation and interaction orchestration. component manages rich media lifecycles, pluginManager handles plugin registration, commandDispatcher routes button clicks to plugins, history manages undo/redo, and shortcuts maps keyboard commands.
DocsApi.layerL3PanelDesc: UI presentation layer. toolbar renders the main toolbar, subToolbar is an optional second toolbar instance, menu handles dropdowns and selection effects, and viewer controls view modes (code view, fullscreen, preview).

Troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
Troubleshooting.subtitle: Fixes for the problems developers run into most often when adding SunEditor to an app.
Troubleshooting.searchPlaceholder: Search by error message or symptom
Troubleshooting.noResults: No matching problems. Try different words, or open an issue below.
Troubleshooting.openPrefilledIssue: Open an issue with your environment pre-filled
Troubleshooting.notListedDesc: Search the existing issues or open a new one with a Playground link that reproduces it.

ssr.title: “window is not defined” during server rendering
ssr.symptom: The build or the server render fails with ReferenceError: window is not defined (Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix).
ssr.cause: SunEditor reads window, document and navigator as soon as the module is imported, so it cannot be imported on the server.
ssr.fix: Import and create the editor only in the browser. In the Next.js App Router, put the editor in a client component and load it with next/dynamic and ssr: false. In Nuxt, wrap it in ClientOnly; in SvelteKit, import it inside onMount.

plugin.title: Error: “The button name of a plugin that does not exist”
plugin.symptom: suneditor.create throws [SUNEDITOR.create.toolbar.fail] The button name of a plugin that does not exist. [image]
plugin.cause: A name in buttonList refers to a plugin that was not passed in the plugins option.
plugin.fix: Pass every plugin, or import just the plugins your toolbar uses and pass those.

target.title: Error: “Cannot find target element” or “The first parameter "target" is missing”
target.symptom: suneditor.create throws [SUNEDITOR.create.fail]-[document.querySelector(#editor)] Cannot find target element, or [SUNEDITOR.create.fail] The first parameter "target" is missing.
target.cause: The target element did not exist yet when the editor was created — the selector matched nothing, or the ref was still null.
target.fix: Create the editor after the component mounts (useEffect, onMounted, ngAfterViewInit, onMount) and pass the element itself instead of a selector.

strictMode.title: The editor is created twice in React development mode
strictMode.symptom: In development the toolbar is duplicated, or the editor flickers on mount.
strictMode.cause: React StrictMode runs effects twice (mount, unmount, mount). Without a cleanup, the second run creates another instance.
strictMode.fix: Return a cleanup from the effect that calls destroy(). The Getting Started examples use this pattern.

css.title: The editor renders without styles
css.symptom: The toolbar appears as an unstyled list and icons or dropdowns are misplaced.
css.cause: The stylesheet is shipped separately from the JavaScript and has not been loaded.
css.fix: Import suneditor/css/editor once in your app, plus suneditor/css/contents for content styles. With the CDN build, add the stylesheet link tags.

contents.title: Saved HTML looks different outside the editor
contents.symptom: Content looks right while editing, but loses spacing, table borders or alignment on the page that displays it.
contents.cause: Content styles live in a separate stylesheet and are scoped to the sun-editor-editable class.
contents.fix: Import suneditor/css/contents on the display page and wrap the HTML in an element with the sun-editor-editable class. Sanitize untrusted HTML on the server before rendering it.

stripped.title: Tags, attributes or styles disappear from the content
stripped.symptom: HTML set with the value option or editor.$.html.set(), or pasted in, comes back without some tags (such as mark), class names, data-* attributes, inline styles or links to custom app schemes (such as zoommtg: or vscode:).
stripped.cause: SunEditor filters all incoming HTML against allow lists for elements, attributes, class names and per-tag styles, and removes anything that is not on them. A span left without any style is unwrapped.
stripped.fix: Extend the allow list you need: elementWhitelist for tags, attributeWhitelist for attributes, allowedClassName for class names, tagStyles for inline styles and allowedURLProtocols for custom URL schemes. Individual filters can also be switched off with the strictMode option. Never allow script tags or on* event attributes.

paste.title: Pasted content loses its formatting, or brings in unwanted styles
paste.symptom: Content pasted from Word, Google Docs or a web page looks different from the source — or you want to accept plain text only.
paste.cause: Pasted HTML goes through the same filtering as any other content. Word and Google Docs markup is cleaned first, then tags, attributes and styles outside the allow lists are removed.
paste.fix: Allow the styles you want to keep with tagStyles (see the previous section). To control pasting yourself, use the onPaste event: it receives the cleaned HTML (data) and its source (from: MS, GOOGLE, SE or empty). Return a string to replace the pasted content, or false to cancel.

value.title: Changing the value prop does not update the editor
value.symptom: You set new HTML in state, but the editor keeps showing the old content.
value.cause: The value option is read once, when the editor is created.
value.fix: Call editor.$.html.set(html) to replace the content and listen to the onChange event to read edits. Do not write the content back from inside onChange — that creates an update loop and moves the caret.

upload.title: Images are saved as huge base64 strings, or uploads are not inserted
upload.symptom: Saved HTML contains long data:image/... strings, or the upload request succeeds but no image appears.
upload.cause: Without image.uploadUrl, images are embedded as base64. With it, the server response must match the format SunEditor expects.
upload.fix: Set image.uploadUrl and return JSON with a result array of url, name and size. Return errorMessage to report a failure. If your API returns a different shape, map it in the imageUploadHandler event.

customUpload.title: Uploading straight to S3 or other storage (presigned URL)
customUpload.symptom: Files should go to S3, Cloudinary or another storage service, so a single image.uploadUrl endpoint does not fit.
customUpload.cause: image.uploadUrl posts files to one endpoint and expects SunEditor's response format.
customUpload.fix: Handle the upload in the onImageUploadBefore event: upload each file yourself, insert it with $.plugins.image.submitURL(url), and return false so SunEditor skips its own upload. submitURL fires the same event again with info.url set — let that call through.

contentApi.title: “editor.getContents is not a function”
contentApi.symptom: Code written for v2 throws TypeError: editor.getContents is not a function (or setContents, appendContents, insertHTML).
contentApi.cause: In v3 the content methods moved to the $.html module, and other v2 instance methods moved to modules such as $.ui.
contentApi.fix: Use the v3 equivalents below. For options and events, use the converter on the Migration page.

v2.title: Options from v2 stopped working after upgrading
v2.symptom: After moving to v3, some options, buttons or events have no effect.
v2.cause: v3 renamed or moved many options — for example, upload options are now nested under the plugin name (image.uploadUrl).
v2.fix: Paste your v2 options into the converter on the Migration page to get the v3 equivalents.
